title: Antihypertensive Medication Classes
general_purpose: Antihypertensive medications are commonly used to lower blood pressure, reduce vascular resistance, and protect against long-term stroke and heart strain.
medication_classes: Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers / ARBs (e.g. Losartan, Telmisartan)
safety_considerations: Choice of blood pressure medication depends on kidney function, heart rate, age, and co-existing medical conditions.
contraindications_warnings: ACE inhibitors and ARBs must not be used during pregnancy. Diuretics require routine electrolyte and kidney function monitoring.
clinician_discussion_points: Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist which blood pressure class best aligns with your blood pressure targets and medical history.

title: Statin & Lipid-Lowering Therapy
general_purpose: Lipid-lowering medications help decrease LDL ('bad') cholesterol, stabilize arterial plaques, and lower long-term risk of coronary heart disease events.
medication_classes: HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors / Statins (e.g. Atorvastatin, Rosuvastatin)
safety_considerations: Statins are widely prescribed for primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention when elevated lipid risk is identified.
contraindications_warnings: Statins are contraindicated during pregnancy and active liver disease. Report unexplainable muscle aches or weakness to a clinician.
clinician_discussion_points: Ask your healthcare provider if a lipid panel review and cardiovascular risk discussion is appropriate for your profile.

title: Blood Glucose & Antidiabetic Agents
general_purpose: Antidiabetic medications help regulate blood glucose levels, improve insulin sensitivity, and protect small and large blood vessels.
safety_considerations: Metformin is typically first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes management alongside lifestyle modifications.
contraindications_warnings: Severe kidney impairment requires dosage adjustment or medication switching. Watch for signs of hypoglycemia when combined with sulfonylureas or insulin.
clinician_discussion_points: Discuss HbA1c screening and fasting blood glucose targets with your clinician.

title: Antiplatelet Therapy Awareness
general_purpose: Antiplatelet therapy reduces blood platelet aggregation to prevent blood clot formation in narrow or hardened arteries.
safety_considerations: Antiplatelets are prescribed based on individualized cardiovascular risk vs bleeding risk evaluation.
contraindications_warnings: Never start daily aspirin for heart protection without explicit doctor authorization due to gastrointestinal bleeding and hemorrhagic stroke risks.
clinician_discussion_points: Inquire with your doctor whether antiplatelet benefit outweighs bleeding risk for your specific profile.
